diagnostic_evidence.quote: the product $v_0 v_1 v_2^2 \approx \tau^{\frac{3}{2}} \e^{-\tau (|x-x_0|^2 + (t-t_0)^2)}$ near the point $(x_0, t_0)$

H_1^{\tau, \theta, (x_0, t_0)}(x,t) &:= H((t-t_0) - \theta \cdot (x - x_0)),\\
    H_2^{\tau, \theta, (x_0, t_0)}(x,t) &:= H((t-t_0) + \theta \cdot (x - x_0)),\\
    H_3^{\tau, \theta, (x_0, t_0)}(x,t) &:= H((t-t_0) - \theta^{\perp} \cdot (x - x_0)),

issues.failure_explanation: With s=t-t_0, a=\theta\cdot(x-x_0), b=\theta^\perp\cdot(x-x_0), the product v_0 v_1 v_2^2 = H_3 H_1 H_2 equals (cutoffs aside) \tau^{3/2} exp(-\tau[(s-a)^2+(s+a)^2+(s-b)^2]/2) = \tau^{3/2} exp(-\tau[s^2+a^2+(s-b)^2/2]), which is a positive-definite but anisotropic Gaussian, not \tau^{3/2}exp(-\tau(|x-x_0|^2+(t-t_0)^2)). Its integral over R^3 is \sqrt{2}\,\pi^{3/2}, not \pi^{3/2}. Hence Lemma \ref{lemma:approx identity q} (isotropic Gaussian) does not apply as stated, and the correct limit identity is 3!\sqrt{2}\pi^{3/2} q(x_0,t_0) = lim \int_\Sigma f_0 \partial^{(1,2)}\Lambda, i.e. the displayed formula is off by a factor \sqrt{2}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the claimed isotropic approximation by the actual quadratic form, apply an anisotropic (change-of-variables) version of Lemma \ref{lemma:approx identity q}, and correct the constant to 3!\sqrt{2}\pi^{3/2}; alternatively choose waves whose product is isotropic.
issues.overall_effect: The pointwise reconstruction formula \eqref{eq: recoequ pw} is quantitatively false; any implementation using its constant (the comparison pointwise reconstructions in Section 4) rescales q by a factor \sqrt{2}. The Radon-based reconstruction is unaffected since there the product H_1H_2 is exactly isotropic in (x\cdot\theta-\eta, t-t_0).
issues.title: Pointwise reconstruction formula has wrong constant: the three-wave product is not an isotropic Gaussian
issues.why_classification: The stated identity does not survive as written; fixing it needs a small but nontrivial replacement argument (anisotropic Gaussian approximation) and changes the reconstruction constant, though the method and the main Radon results are untouched.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let us now consider the reconstruction of $\radonR(q)$ for a set of parameters $W_0 \in W_{\text{Radon}}$.
We define the admissible reconstruction domain by setting $T>4r$, $t_1>2r$, $t_2<T-2r$
space domain $\Omega = [-0.5, 0.5]^2$ and time domain $[0, T] = [0, 3]$
$P$ corresponds to the interval $[-0.4, 0.4]$ divided into $63$ equally spaced distances from the origin

issues.failure_explanation: For \Omega=[-0.5,0.5]^2, r=\sqrt2/2\approx0.707, so W_Radon requires t_0\in(2r,T-2r)=(1.414,1.586). The implementation uses t_0=T/2+\eta_0 with \eta_0\in[-0.4,0.4], i.e. t_0\in[1.1,1.9], violating the paper's own admissibility condition for |\eta_0|>0.086, contradicting the claim W_0\subset W_Radon. The underlying requirement for the integral identity is that v_0 vanish on \Omega at t=T, i.e. |2\eta_0-T/2|>r (plus cutoff width h and Gaussian tails); at \eta_0=0.4 this gives 0.7<0.707 for diagonal \theta_0, so the hypothesis v_0|_{t=T}=\partial_t v_0|_{t=T}=0 used in deriving \eqref{eq: integralidentity: eps general case} is (marginally) not satisfied at the edge of P.

failure_location.quote: for each $\eta_0 \in P$, we set the auxiliary function $v_0$ corresponding to $(\frac{T}{2} + \eta_0, \theta_0, \eta_0)$ as in Section \ref{sec: choosing boundary for radon}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the conservative W_Radon check by the sharper direct conditions |\eta_0-t_0|>r+h and |\eta_0+t_0-T|>r+h (with the square's actual half-width in direction \theta_0), and restrict P (or enlarge T) so that all tuples satisfy them.
issues.overall_effect: The theoretical justification via W_Radon does not cover the parameter range actually reconstructed; for the extreme distances \eta_0 near 0.4 the auxiliary wave may not vanish at t=T, so the integral identity acquires an unaccounted boundary term and the corresponding sinogram entries are not rigorously justified.
issues.title: Numerical Radon parameter tuples lie outside the stated admissible set W_Radon
issues.why_classification: A local verification with sharper sufficient conditions and a slight trimming of P (or larger T) restores the guarantee for all reconstructed tuples without changing the method or results.
